favourite.heading: Why Oklahoma can pull away
bullets: Conference strength differs and the in-season sample is still thin, worth 5.7 points to Oklahoma (+5.7 pts).

Oklahoma is the better football team by 4.8 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 74% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (+4.8 pts).
Playing at Oklahoma is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).
Stylistically the matchup favours Oklahoma by 1.5 points: early-down offence vs early-down defence (+1.5 pts).

underdog.heading: Why New Mexico can keep it close
bullets: The outcome range is 15.3 points wide at one sigma — p10 -7.0 to p90 +37.0 for Oklahoma, so a projection of +16.0 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 4%.

The market disagrees by 5.5 points. The market is not the truth, but a gap that large is more often the model missing information (a suspension, a starter, a scheme change) than the market being wrong.
